_readme: RULE: a source renders as a clickable link ONLY when verified is true.
Everything else renders as plain text. The name is still useful; a broken
link is not. There is no middle state and no 'probably fine'.
WHERE THESE URLS CAME FROM. Every url below was copied from a live web
search result, not written from memory. That distinction is the whole point:
a model reconstructs the SHAPE of a plausible URL rather than recalling a
real one, which is how you end up citing a page that has never existed.
Sources with no url field are ones that could not be confirmed that way.
They are listed by name, unlinked, until someone confirms them.
verified is still false on all of them, because appearing in a search index
is good evidence but not proof the page is live right now. Run:
It probes each url and flips verified only on a live 200. Only then do links
appear on the site. Adding a url by hand without running the check does
Only 404 and 410 mean dead. A 403 is a bot wall and a 5xx is a bad day;
both stay unverified rather than being deleted.
